chunks: The semblance of those who believe not in the life to come is that of the meanest; but the semblance of God is the most sublime, for He is all-mighty and all-wise.

key_terms.السَّوْءِ: The meanest / The lower / The bad
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter / the life to come

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the 'lower example' and the 'highest example' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted through the lens of divine attributes (Sifat), where 'muthal al-saw'' refers to the imperfect, contingent nature of creation or the specific qualities of disbelievers, contrasted with God's absolute perfection. The phrase 'wa huwa al-'aziz al-hakim' underscores that this distinction is not arbitrary but rooted in God's omnipotence and wisdom, affirming that His 'highest example' encompasses all perfections without limitation. This contrast serves as a theological reminder that human understanding of God is limited by our own imperfect nature, whereas His essence remains transcendent and supreme.
